meaning.value: The true name of the player's amulet: an ancient diplomatic envoy artifact that translates all languages, opens diplomatic roads and sealed gates, recalls an injured bearer, and transfers objects between realms.
The protagonist's self-appointed rename of the Amulet of Concord. Canon: his invention, reflecting his delusion; no one else uses this name.

The ten peaceful realms behind the ancient enchanted gates, at peace for roughly ten thousand years. Skeletons, goblins, living flames, dryads, and stranger creatures maintaining marshes, oceans, deserts, and mountains.
A millennia-old children's adventure comedy whose "villains" are affectionate caricatures of the realms' rulers. The protagonist mistakes it for an ancient prophecy.
The realms' one ancient moral law: no blow may fall before its path has been shown. The reason telegraphs never lie and every attack pattern has a learnable movement answer.
The ancient restorative magic sustaining the Ten Realms. It reconstructs the dead — restoring the body but keeping pain and memory — so the isolated realms can never be permanently destroyed.
An ancient diplomatic device in the hub that lets people observe events beyond the gates in real time. Built to protect envoys; now it lets hub NPCs watch everything the player does.

An ancient inter-realm emergency service responding to fires, floods, collapsed buildings, and dangerous animals. Their large silhouette is deliberately recognizable so civilians know help has arrived.
The hero's label for a Heavy Hand. In truth each one is an emergency responder carrying a gate seal as credentials — the player's horde "trophy".
The inhabitants' word for the shared agricultural grounds, memorial spaces, wetlands, and ceremonial plazas the hero calls "battlefields". Horde waves are residents arriving to contain an intruder.

Fragments of damaged domestic magic: heating stones, irrigation runes, memorial lamps, protective charms, workshop enchantments, and Continuance splinters. The hero calls them concentrated evil and uses them to improve his weapons.

The hero's word for gate seals taken from senior wardens and emergency responders. He believes elite monsters carried keys to darker territories; in truth he is stripping credentials off rescue workers.

Holding E to make the amulet transfer carried loot out through the diplomatic network, beyond its owners' reach. The hero calls it securing dangerous materials; the inhabitants call it theft. Dying before banking lets owners recover their property.
A credential carried by senior wardens and emergency responders identifying someone trusted to cross realm boundaries during a crisis. Fed into the amulet, seals force gates open.

The window when a guardian becomes exhausted from maintaining defenses — protecting civilians, reinforcing barriers, buying time for evacuation. The hero reads exhaustion as divine judgment revealing evil's weakness.
A goblin festival underway in the Palisade Camp when the hero first arrives. The Goblin War Crown greets him as a stranger who has entered mid-celebration.

The hero's term for everything he takes from optional treasure detours — in truth family storehouses, ceremonial treasuries, pantries, memorial chambers, workshops, diplomatic gifts, and emergency supplies.
